newsitem.title: USA: PC stocks fall as Gateway Q2 disappoints.
newsitem.headline: PC stocks fall as Gateway Q2 disappoints.

text.p: Investors lost some enthusiasm for skyrocketing personal computer stocks after Gateway 2000 Inc reported an on-target second quarter but with some disappointing elements that provided an excuse to sell.

"Everyone is using the Gateway report as an excuse to sell," said Louis Mazzucchelli, a Gerard Klauer & Mattison analyst. "Gateway had two inventory issues, one of their own making and one aided by Intel. The Pentium II transition caught them flat-footed." Gateway's Q2 was on track at $0.36.
Some analysts said investors are nervous that Gateway's inventory build-up is a signal that PC demand is slowing.
But analysts said that Gateway's inventory issues were Gateway-specific and that they were not worried about the outlook for the big PC players in the third quarter.

The shares of the leading PC makers were all down, after reaching new highs this week, in a euphoric frenzy for PC shares, especially Dell Computer Corp. Dell was off 6-3/4 to 163-1/4, Compaq Computer Corp tumbled 4-1/4 to 136-5/8 and Gateway 2000 eased 2-5/16 to 40-7/8.
"It could be a one day correction, people are taking some profits," said Daniel Kunstler, a J.P. Morgan analyst, who downgraded Gateway earlier Friday to a market performer.

"To justify the valuation (of Gateway) we need the potential upside in earnings," he said, adding that while Gateway's growth is very robust, it appears to be trailing that of its major competitors, Compaq and Dell.

Daniel Ries, a Nomura Securities analyst, said that in recent days PC stocks have also been surging as investors anticipate PC market research data, which is due to be published by International Data Corp and Dataquest Monday.
"These things can't go up forever," said one trader, adding that there has been major short covering. "When the short covers walk away, there aren't many buyers out there."
"The stock has gone through the roof," said Kunstler, referring to Dell, which has almost tripled in price since January, when it was trading at around 57.

Kunstler said that he has no major fundamental issues with Dell, such as he does with Gateway, and has no changes in his earnings outlook, saying he is the high on the street and his view has not changed.
